newsitem.title: UK: LME copper extends gains, hits new 13-month highs.
newsitem.headline: LME copper extends gains, hits new 13-month highs.

text.p: Speculative interest carried copper prices to fresh 13-month highs on Thursday and the market was eyeing $2,600 as the next level, traders said.
Three months copper raced up to $2,593 per tonne in pre-market trading, compared to Wednesday's kerb close of $2,561.
Dealers said the buying was largely technical in nature.
"When you've got the funds and institutions buying, it builds a momentum all its own, even though fundamentals are quiet ahead of the summer season," a traders said.
The widening backwardation in nearby dates was helping to fuel the rally, traders said. July/threes and August/threes were attracting the most interest.
Cash to threes backwardation was last quoted at $110/115, some $10 wider than on Wednesday and out by around $50 from the start of the week.
On the supply side, the market was watching Inco's ongoing Sudbury strike and especially shipping problems at the Ok Tedi mine in Papua New Guinea.

The possibilty of prolonged delays in copper concentrate shipments from Ok Tedi, which is being plagued by low water levels and fuel shortages, was already boosting spot concentrate prices, Far East traders said.
The other base metals were virtually ignored.
Aluminium was quoted just firmer at $1,625/1,626, compared to $1,623 at the previous close.
Steady LME stock drawdowns continued with little effect, with inventories decreasing by 3,100 tonnes.

"Aluminium has been a little disappointing. The funds are flat, after getting out last week, and they don't want to get back in," a trader said. "Zinc is also sidelined by the funds in favour of copper."
Zinc prices edged lower after LME stocks rose by 2,225 tonnes, which traders said was most likely Chinese material entering Singapore warehouses. It was last at $1,365, off $3.
Lead was little changed at $638, up $1, and nickel was quiet at $7,280/7,290, versus $7,260.
Nickel was likely to find support at $7,200, analysts said.
Tin was indicated slightly firmer at $5,630/5,640, from $5,600.
Alloy was quoted at $1,480/1,490, compared to $1,486/1,490.
